(By The Court U/S 26 Of Land Acquisition Act- 1894 On Reference
Petition U/S 18 Of The Act):
1.

This reference under section 18 of The Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was sent to this
court by the Land Acquisition Collector qua Award No.01/2011-2012.

2.  As per the LAC Award, a large tract of land measuring 3822 sq. meters of village Azadpur, Delhi, was acquired by the Govt. for a public purpose i.e. "Construction of Grade Separator at Azadpur, under Planned Development of Delhi".
Notification under Section 4 of The Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as 'LA Act') was issued on 18.04.2007.
Declaration under Section 6 was made on 11.01.2008.

Thereafter, Award bearing no.
01/2011-2012/DC (NW) was announced by Land Acquisition Collector (hereinafter referred to as LAC) on 05.05.2011.
The LAC determined the market price of the acquired land as Rs.16,613/- per square meter.
LAC No. 148/17 page 2 of 8 SIDHARTH MATHUR MATHUR Date: 2025.12.06
The petitioner being dissatisfied with the market value determined by the LAC, filed the present petition u/s 18 of the LA Act, seeking reference to this court.
The Land Acquisition Collector forwarded the same to this court, for adjudication.

4. The petitioner's case in brief is that the petitioner was the owner /occupant and was in possession of the land bearing Khasra numbers as mentioned in the Statement u/s 19 of the LA Act that was annexed with the present reference and admitted by the petitioner during the stage of admission/denial of documents, situated within the of Village Azadpur, Delhi (the said land).
The said land was acquired vide notification dated 18.04.2007.

5. The petitioner has challenged the said award inter alia on the ground of inadequacy of compensation and incorrect assessment of market value of land inter-alia due to non-consideration of relevant factors like potentiality and fertility of the suit land, the surrounding colonies and developed areas, the market value of the adjoining areas /villages, the sale deeds of other lands of the contemporary period, nearness to the National Highway and industrial areas, the amenities available in the suit land etc.
6.

The petitioner has prayed compensation at enhanced LAC No. 148/17 page 3 of 8 SIDHARTH SIDHARTH MATHUR MATHUR Date: 2025.12.06 16:06:50 +0530 rate besides interest thereon and solatium in addition to the compensation.

sentences.text:
7. The respondent no.1/the Union of India (UOI)/Land Acquisition Collector and respondent no.
2/PWD contested the reference petition by filing their respective Written Statements.

8. The petition has been contested mainly on the ground that the LAC awarded adequate compensation to the petitioner after taking into consideration all the relevant factors and therefore,
LAC has correctly assessed the market value of the land after taking into account the market rates prevailing at the time of notification under Section 4 of LA Act.

In Written Statement, R-2/PWD has adopted the contention of R-1/UOI.
9.
During admission-denial of documents, the counsel for petitioner admitted the statement given u/s 19 of the Act.

The following issues were framed:-
i) Whether the petitioner is entitled to enhancement in compensation, if so, at what rate ?
OPP ii) Relief.

10. In evidence, on instructions of the petitioner, the counsel for petitioner has relied upon the judgment in a LAC No. 148/17 page 4 of 8 SIDHARTH SIDHARTH MATHUR Date: 2025.12.06 16:06:56 +0530 case Jai Bhagwan Gupta Vs. UOI, LAC No. 38/17 DOD- 07.05.2025 and also the evidence led in said case.
11.

entities.text: Jai Bhagwan Gupta Vs. UOI, LAC No. 38/17
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondent no.1/Union of India, in its evidence, tendered the award as Ex. R1 in evidence.
However, no one has appeared on behalf of the R-2/PWD despite repeated calls.

Accordingly, its right to lead RE was closed on 04.12.2025.
12.
I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have also carefully considered the record.

My issue-wise findings are given as under:-
FINDINGS ON ISSUE NO. 1 :-
13.
Petitioner has contended that valuation of land determined by LAC is not reasonable as LAC has not adopted the correct method of valuation.
However, he has not led any evidence to show as to how the LAC was wrong in fixing market value of land.

Ld. Counsel for the petitioner has only relied upon the judgment titled as Jai Bhagwan Gupta Vs. UOI & Anr., LAC No. 38/17, decided by Sh.
Deepak Dabas, Ld. Predecessor of this Court on 07.05.2025 conceded that award be passed in terms of the said judgment and the same enhancement which was granted in the said judgment be also granted to petitioner.
14.

entities.text: Jai Bhagwan Gupta Vs. UOI & Anr., LAC No. 38/17
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Jai Bhagwan Gupta's case (Supra), an elaborate LAC No. 148/17 page 5 of 8 SIDHARTH MATHUR MATHUR Date: 2025.12.06 16:07:01 +0530 and detailed discussion was made before determining the amount of compensation.

With respect to the land of the village Azadpur (involved herein), acquired through the same notification (as made herein), the Ld. Predecessor of this Court Manish Gupta vs U.O.I.And Ors on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27933342/
3 determined the market value of the land as Rs. 27,000/- per square meter.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. Since, no different evidence has been led by the petitioner in the present case, I have no reason to give a different treatment to the land of the petitioner and to give a determination, different from that determined in the Jai Bhagwan Gupta's case (Supra).
The fair market value of the acquired land is adjudicated as Rs. 27,000/- per square meter as determined in Jai Bhagwan Gupta's case (Supra).
Accordingly, I hold that the petitioner would be entitled to market value @ Rs. 27,000/- per square meter.
16. Petitioner has also claimed compensation for crops, tree, tubewell etc.
However, the petitioner has failed to lead any evidence to substantiate his claim or to establish that he was not awarded sufficient compensation for same.

Accordingly, I hold that petitioner is not entitled to any enhancement in compensation on this count.
17.

Besides above, petitioner shall be entitled to other statutory benefits under the LA Act viz. 12%
additional LAC No. 148/17 page 6 of 8 SIDHARTH MATHUR MATHUR Date: 2025.12.06 16:07:05 +0530 amount [as per section 23 (1A)] and 30% solatium [u/s 23 (2)] and will be entitled to interest under Section 28 of L.A Act on the fair market value @ 9% per annum for the first year and @ 15%
for subsequent year till the making of payment of enhanced compensation by LAC as per provision of Section 28 of the Act.
Issue no. 1 is decided accordingly.
18. Findings on Issue No.2 - RELIEF

The share(s) of the petitioner(s) would be determinable as per the statement u/s 19 of the L.A.
Act proved on record and the said statement shall constitute a part of this award.

4. interest under Section 28 of L.A Act @ 9% per annum for the first year from the date of dispossession and at the rate of 15% per annum on the difference between the enhanced compensation LAC No. 148/17 page 7 of 8 SIDHARTH SIDHARTH MATHUR MATHUR Date: 2025.12.06 16:07:10 +0530 awarded by this court and the compensation awarded by the LAC for the subsequent period till its payment ;
